account: It is day 1, about 09:14. I have kept my eight o'clock office appointment and arrived outside the mill early for the ten o'clock grain inspection. The secretary found nobody at the mill last evening or this morning, so the inspection is scheduled but arrangements remain unconfirmed. That is the main unusual circumstance I know of; I do not yet know why staff were absent or who manages the records. The secretary's inquiries to the baker and innkeeper did not identify a records manager, and freight gave no answer before the secretary left. I requested existing grain stock and delivery records, shortages, and storage concerns for the inspection, not movement of supplies. There is no evidence yet of an actual shortage or wrongdoing. Several townsfolk are nearby on the east bank, but I could not make out their recent conversations and cannot infer their purposes. Yesterday people reported the baker carrying wheat, and my tea host described fresh loaves being prepared for market; that sounds consistent with ordinary bakery business. No new correspondence had reached the secretary this morning. After the inspection, my appointments are lunch at home at noon, council letters at thirteen, tea at the confirmed dockside cottage at fifteen, office at sixteen-thirty, and home at nineteen.
